subject: Acme TCO post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-12T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Acme TCO post-call recap & next steps

Hey Jordan —

Thanks again for the time today. Wanted to capture the key items we discussed and surface the immediate TCO levers so your finance team has a concise starting point. I’ve attached the workbook we ran through (acme-tco-workbook.xlsx) and a 1‑pager pricing summary.

Summary (what you told us)
- Pain: token spend is the largest variable cost; peak latency on customer-facing chat needs to stay <500ms P95.
- Goals: reduce inference cost by 40-60% vs current self-hosted flow, maintain quality and latency SLAs, and get a procurement-friendly pricing view for FY27 budgeting.
- Current constraints: budget headroom ~$120k/Q for inference; procurement requires an itemized cost model and SOC2 evidence.

TCO levers we discussed
1) Token economics: sample assumptions in workbook — baseline 120M prompt+completion tokens/mo; current unit cost (self-hosted) ~= $X per 1M tokens when accounting infra/ops. Redwood hosted delta pricing shown in the attachment.
2) Batching & utilization: enabling continuous batching on your request pattern should improve GPU utilization and reduce per-token runtime cost by ~20-30% depending on concurrency.
3) KV/prefix caching: for repeat prompts and system/prefix content we expect a cache hit rate improvement to cut downstream tokens by ~15-25% after warmup (we show a conservative 15% in the workbook).
4) Quantization & model selection: switching to the recommended quantized variant for the assistant reduces runtime and memory footprint; model delta + batching yields further savings.

Estimated savings (conservative model in workbook)
- Estimated net reduction in inference unit cost: ~45% (combination of batching, caching, and model profile).
- Estimated monthly $ savings: see "Summary" tab in workbook; we included a best/likely/conservative column for your execs.

Next steps
- I’ll share an updated workbook with token-level breakouts and a one-page summary for procurement (attached).
- Can we schedule a 30-min call with your finance/procurement team next week to review assumptions and procurement items? Rafael (cc’d) will join to cover pricing and contract options (reserved capacity vs committed usage).
- If useful, we can run a 7-day pilot traffic slice to validate cache hit rates and latency impact.

Attachments: acme-tco-workbook.xlsx, redwood-pricing-1pager.pdf

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

--
Marissa Cole
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before I loop finance/procurement:

1) Token assumptions: can you call out the assumed average prompt vs completion split per session (we have longer completions for summaries)?
2) The workbook shows a 45% reduction — can you outline what portion of that is from software optimizations (batching/caching) vs model/quantization changes? Procurement will want to know how much is recurring software behavior vs one-time engineering work (pilot/integration).

Also: procurement asked whether Redwood can provide a short pilot SOW and a pricing attachment we can hand to our vendor team. If you can share those and a SOC2 link, that will expedite review.

Jordan — good questions. Short answers and where to find the detail in the workbook: 

1) Prompt vs completion split
- Workbook assumptions ("Traffic" tab): average prompt = 400 tokens, average completion = 1,800 tokens per session (we used your example of long summaries). We also included a sensitivity table at 1k/1k and 500/1500 tokens to show impact.

2) Savings decomposition
- Software/operational levers (batching + caching + routing optimizations): ~25-30% of cost reduction in the conservative scenario. These are recurring improvements and don't require model changes.
- Model/quantization + instance-level runtime: ~15-20% additional reduction. Quantized model variants reduce GPU cycles per token; combined with better utilization this is additive.
- We flagged one-time integration items (pilot, instrumentation) in the workbook under "Implementation" with an estimated 1-2 week engineering effort.

3) Pilot SOW & procurement items
- Attached: redwood-pricing-1pager.pdf (pricing lines + billing terms). I’ll follow up with a short pilot SOW template and a SOC2 link.

4) Actionable next steps
- Rafael to propose pricing options (committed vs burst capacity) and a procurement-friendly quote.
- Marissa to schedule a 30-min call w/ your finance/procurement (please propose two slots).
- Optionally: approve 7-day pilot slice to measure cache hit and latency — we can run this with limited traffic and a simple metrics dashboard.

Links: Pilot workbook & modeling sheet: https://drive.google.com/spreadsheets/d/ACME-TCO-WORKBOOK
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/ACME

Marissa
